verdicts.trueWording: differ enough that I do not like to offer one
verdicts.note: Raw Wayback capture (200, 4,993 words). Opening paragraph: she declines the substitute Jussi offered, then gives the two by-lines' style and topic as the reason, with a restaurant simile. Both limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the details of raising chickens or putting a roof on a house
verdicts.note: Paragraph after the Alaska section, on hands-on experience and suspension of disbelief; the dragons half of the sentence is the recounting of dragons' habits. Quote is contiguous on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: not just in research, but in attempting to experience the things
verdicts.note: Same paragraph, immediately after the chickens sentence; the page continues that this is so as to include the physical details in the stories. Every limb supported.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the first Farseer book' - the page names the book only by its working title, Chivalry's Bastard, and never calls it a Farseer book
verdicts.trueWording: to attempt a completely different sort of voice and telling
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim in the pen-name section, alongside her decision to write it in the first person; the Farseer identification is an outside inference. The page's only Farseer mentions are the later tenth book set in a different universe and Fitz and the Fool.

verdicts.trueWording: escape the limits that I had placed on myself
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the paragraph on reactions to the name change. The 'not an editor' limb is carried by the earlier Gypsy paragraph, which says it was she binding herself to a style and not any editorial pressure.

verdicts.trueWording: a theatre, a grocery store, a library, the post office
verdicts.note: Tacoma/Proctor District paragraph: the list is what she can walk to from her home, continuing 'and various retail stores'. Bare-list form and the neighbourhood framing both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Our population is about 193,000 people, median age 33
verdicts.note: Tacoma paragraph, verbatim. The foreign-readership limb is the piece's own header: written for Alienisti, Finncon 2004.

verdicts.trueWording: each year we raised a couple of pigs for slaughter
verdicts.note: Midlist paragraph: the same sentences name Roy, Washington, the mid-list years as Megan Lindholm, chickens, ducks, geese, pigeons and a garden. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: think that today you will write a scene
verdicts.note: Closing advice paragraph; the contrast limb is the preceding sentence, that deciding to sit down and write a book is the mistake. Framed on the page as her best advice.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the piece that won her an A' - the page gives the A as a course grade and only says the instructor praised the piece; it also scopes the class to the one she took at Denver University
verdicts.trueWording: long on character and short on plot
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the Denver paragraph, and 'not a story, because nothing really happened' is on the page. The grade attribution and the unrestricted 'her only creative-writing class' are the widened limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: little more snarky, a little more sarcastic, a little less optimistic
verdicts.note: Live Guardian page fetched raw with a browser UA (200). Pen-name section: the voice she was writing in was very different from Megan Lindholm, who is thus described; the page adds 'less emotional', which the claim omits without distortion.

verdicts.trueWording: Fitz is cagey, he doesn’t always admit the full truth
verdicts.note: Same quoted run, ending 'about anything, but he really says what he's feeling'. The narrator limb is supported earlier: the book is told in Fitz's voice.

verdicts.trueWording: the Fool had exactly one sentence in the outline
verdicts.note: Fool paragraph, opening 'When I first began writing the book'; the same quote ends with him becoming one of the major characters. The book is Assassin's Apprentice, named on the page as her first as Robin Hobb.

verdicts.trueWording: lowering the threshold of disbelief so the reader can step right
verdicts.note: Paragraph after the Martin 'diamonds' line; the quote continues into the book and not feeling blocked out. Attribution on the page is 'Good fantasy, Hobb believes', with the definition itself in her words.

verdicts.trueWording: And I think silly is more dangerous than impossible
verdicts.note: Closing sentence of the same quoted run, verbatim; the fantasy framing is the sentence it caps, about what would block a reader out.
